title: Canonical integral-to-adic coefficient tower map
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a scheme $T$. Use the system convention of [def-sp-tower-class-reduction] and the ring of integers quotients $A_{n,T}=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^{n+1})_T$ of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Define $R_{n,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1})_T$ and its quotient transitions. The map $R_{n,T}\to A_{n,T}$ is the constant sheaf map induced by the unique unital integer quotient map; $\ell^{n+1}=0$ in the latter quotient, and these maps commute with transitions. Their ringed sequence-site map is the canonical coefficient-system map. Its unit-module map under restriction of scalars is uniquely characterized on every section by this very ring map. Exponents are positive; the index zero denotes exponent one, and ramification does not change $\ell$ into a uniformizer.
